images.alt:
ASCII-art diagram titled "One token by telegraph", showing how one transformer layer would be computed by a fictional civilisation. At the top, a skyline drawing depicts the Capital — a city of 1,000,000 core scribes — connected by roughly 300 km of telegraph wire (100 bits per second, signals at 0.7c) to the Towns, where 10,000,000 more scribes work.
Below the skyline is a timeline for computing one layer (layer k of 120, processed strictly in order), with two parallel columns: the Capital (one million scribes, 10 km wide) and the Towns (ten million scribes, 300 km out). The timeline reads:
Hour 0.0: the Capital begins self-attention. This happens in the core only, because every desk may need to read the whole token census. Half the city is on duty at any time, in two 12-hour shifts. It takes 9.4 hours of arithmetic plus 1.8 hours of keying messages across the city's own wires, finishing at hour 11.3.
Hour 11.3: the Capital transmits the MLP inputs for layer k to the Towns — 327 kilobits, about 0.9 hours of keying. The 300 km of light-lag adds only 1.4 milliseconds.
Hour 12.2: both sides compute the MLP feed-forward in step. The Towns' ten million desks each work on their own slice, no town consulting another; the Capital's on-duty half joins with its own share. This takes 0.9 hours.
Hour 13.0: the Towns key the MLP outputs back to the Capital — another 327 kilobits, 0.9 hours.
Hour 13.9: the Capital performs the residual add and normalisation and files the layer record (negligible time). The hidden state then passes to layer k+1, back to the top of the cycle, while the towns sit idle until the next dispatch keys in.

A towering biomechanical monstrosity rises from a sprawling mound of decaying machinery, skeletal remains, tangled cables, and industrial debris. Its massive upper body is assembled from corroded metal, exposed bones, rotting organic tissue, hoses, wires, and twisted mechanical components. At the center, an enormous skull-like head leans forward with a partially open jaw filled with broken, uneven teeth. One eye socket is dark while the other contains a small glowing amber light.
Thick ribbed tubing emerges from the creature’s face and neck, connecting its decayed anatomy to the surrounding mechanical structure. Two enormous segmented appendages curve upward behind its shoulders like the skeletal tails of prehistoric creatures, ending in jagged, blade-like formations. Countless wires and thin cables extend outward from the body, creating the appearance of exposed nerves or invasive mechanical roots.
The creature’s long, asymmetrical arms hang toward the ground. One side appears heavily fused with a smaller skeletal figure and rusted machinery, while the opposite limb is thin and elongated. Translucent strands of wet material and decay hang from the torso and appendages. The surrounding landscape is covered with heaps of refuse, broken equipment, bones, and dark standing water. Pale industrial structures disappear into a cold, foggy background, emphasizing the immense scale of the creature and the bleak, contaminated environment.
